subject: maths
title: Converting Units
seo_title: Year 6 Converting Units Worksheets: Decimals, Time, Miles and Kilometres (Free, with Answers)
standard_text: Solve problems involving the calculation and conversion of units of measure, using decimal notation up to three decimal places where appropriate; use, read, write and convert between standard units, converting measurements of length, mass, volume and time from a smaller unit of measure to a larger unit, and vice versa, using decimal notation to up to three decimal places; convert between miles and kilometres.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on converting units: length, mass and capacity with decimals to three places, time, and miles and kilometres (5 miles ≈ 8 km). Scales, conversion graphs and SATs-style word problems. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the National Curriculum.
key_big: Bigger unit to smaller unit: multiply. Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide.
key_sub: × or ÷ 1,000 moves the digits 3 places: 2.375 kg = 2,375 g and 45 mm = 0.045 m. Time uses 60, so 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes. And 5 miles ≈ 8 km.
body_html:
Multiply or divide?

To change a bigger unit into a smaller unit, multiply: you need more of the small units. To change a smaller unit into a bigger unit, divide. Multiplying by 1,000 moves every digit 3 places to the left. Dividing by 1,000 moves every digit 3 places to the right.

Kilograms to grams

2.375 kg = ☐ g

1 kg = 1,000 g. Multiply: 2.375 × 1,000 = 2,375.

Answer: 2,375 g

Millimetres to metres

45 mm = ☐ m

1 m = 1,000 mm. Divide: 45 ÷ 1,000 = 0.045. Use 0 as a place holder in the tenths.

Answer: 0.045 m

Facts to know

MeasureFacts
Length1 cm = 10 mm   1 m = 100 cm = 1,000 mm   1 km = 1,000 m
Mass1 kg = 1,000 g
Capacity1 l = 1,000 ml
Time1 minute = 60 seconds   1 hour = 60 minutes   1 day = 24 hours   1 week = 7 days
Miles5 miles ≈ 8 km (so 1 mile ≈ 1.6 km)

Time is not decimal

An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. Multiply the decimal part by 60.

Hours and minutes

2.5 hours = ☐ hours ☐ minutes

0.5 × 60 = 30 minutes.

Answer: 2 hours 30 minutes (not 2 hours 50 minutes)

Seconds to minutes

210 seconds = ☐ minutes ☐ seconds

3 × 60 = 180. 210 − 180 = 30 seconds left over.

Answer: 3 minutes 30 seconds

Miles and kilometres

A mile is longer than a kilometre. Use 5 miles ≈ 8 km like a ratio: find how many lots of 5 miles (or 8 km) there are, then multiply.

Miles to kilometres

40 miles ≈ ☐ km

40 ÷ 5 = 8 lots. 8 × 8 = 64.

Answer: about 64 km

Kilometres to miles

24 km ≈ ☐ miles

24 ÷ 8 = 3 lots. 3 × 5 = 15.

Answer: about 15 miles

Read the scale, then convert

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
2.5 hours = 2 hours 50 minutes0.5 hours = half of 60 minutes = 30 minutes
45 mm = 4.5 m or 45 m1 m = 1,000 mm, so 45 mm = 45 ÷ 1,000 = 0.045 m
1.25 l = 125 mlMultiply by 1,000, not 100: 1.25 l = 1,250 ml
Multiplying to get a bigger unit (750 g = 750,000 kg)Smaller unit to bigger unit: divide (750 g = 0.75 kg)
8 miles ≈ 5 km (the wrong way round)A mile is longer, so 5 miles ≈ 8 km
Comparing only the numbers (5,200 cm > 0.5 km)Use one unit first: 5,200 cm = 52 m and 0.5 km = 500 m

faq.q: What unit conversions do Year 6 pupils need to know?
faq.a: Year 6 pupils convert between mm, cm, m and km, g and kg, ml and l, and units of time, using decimals up to three decimal places. They also convert between miles and kilometres.

faq.q: How do you convert miles to kilometres in Year 6?
faq.a: Use 5 miles ≈ 8 km. Find how many lots of 5 miles there are and multiply by 8: 40 miles is 8 lots, so about 64 km.

faq.q: Why is 2.5 hours not 2 hours 50 minutes?
faq.a: An hour has 60 minutes, not 100. 0.5 hours is half an hour, which is 30 minutes, so 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes.

faq.q: Are converting units questions in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. Converting units can come up in the reasoning papers, often in word problems with money, recipes, distances or time, and pupils may need to read scales or conversion graphs.

sets.title: Length: mm, cm, m and km with decimals

items.q: Convert. 45 mm = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Millimetres are smaller than centimetres, so divide by 10: 45 ÷ 10 = 4.5. The digits move 1 place to the right. So 45 mm = 4.5 cm.

items.q: Convert. 3.6 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 3.6 × 100 = 360. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 3.6 m = 360 cm.

items.q: Convert. 2.4 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1,000: 2.4 × 1,000 = 2,400. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.4 km = 2,400 m.

items.q: Convert. 850 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1,000: 850 ÷ 1,000 = 0.85. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 850 m = 0.85 km.

items.q: Convert. 0.6 cm = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 cm = 10 mm. Centimetres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 10: 0.6 × 10 = 6. The digits move 1 place to the left. So 0.6 cm = 6 mm.

items.q: Convert. 1.75 m = ☐ mm
items.e: 1 m = 1,000 mm. Metres are bigger than millimetres, so multiply by 1,000: 1.75 × 1,000 = 1,750. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.75 m = 1,750 mm. (1.75 × 100 = 175 would give centimetres, not millimetres.)

items.q: Convert. 45 mm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 1,000 mm. Millimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 1,000: 45 ÷ 1,000 = 0.045. The digits move 3 places to the right, so you need a 0 in the tenths place. So 45 mm = 0.045 m.

items.q: Convert. 3.125 km = ☐ m
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Kilometres are bigger than metres, so multiply by 1,000: 3.125 × 1,000 = 3,125. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 3.125 km = 3,125 m.

items.q: Convert. 65 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1,000: 65 ÷ 1,000 = 0.065. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 65 m = 0.065 km. Check: 0.65 km would be 650 m.

items.q: Convert. 7 cm = ☐ m
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Centimetres are smaller than metres, so divide by 100: 7 ÷ 100 = 0.07. The digits move 2 places to the right. So 7 cm = 0.07 m.
The pencil ends 3 small marks after 8 cm, so it is 8 cm 3 mm = 83 mm. 1 m = 1,000 mm, so divide by 1,000: 83 ÷ 1,000 = 0.083 m.

items.q: Convert. 4,050 m = ☐ km
items.e: 1 km = 1,000 m. Metres are smaller than kilometres, so divide by 1,000: 4,050 ÷ 1,000 = 4.05. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 4,050 m = 4.05 km. The 0 in 4,050 keeps its place: 4.05, not 4.5.

items.q: Convert. 1.08 m = ☐ cm
items.e: 1 m = 100 cm. Metres are bigger than centimetres, so multiply by 100: 1.08 × 100 = 108. The digits move 2 places to the left. So 1.08 m = 108 cm.

items.q: Convert. 2 km 75 m = ☐ km
Which is the same as 0.305 km?
items.e: Multiply by 1,000: 0.305 × 1,000 = 305 m. The 0 holds the tenths place, so it is not 35 m.

items.q: Which is the same as 6.04 m?
Which is the longest?
items.e: Change them all to metres: 0.5 km = 500 m, 5,200 cm = 52 m and 0.48 km = 480 m. 500 m is the longest. 5,200 cm has the biggest number, but centimetres are small.

items.q: Which is the shortest?
items.e: Change them all to millimetres: 6.5 cm = 65 mm, 0.07 m = 70 mm and 0.6 m = 600 mm. 65 mm is the shortest.

items.q: Which is true?
Find the missing number. 1 km − 375 m = ☐ km

sets.title: Mass and capacity: g, kg, ml and l

items.q: Convert. 1.25 l = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 1.25 × 1,000 = 1,250. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 1.25 l = 1,250 ml. (125 ml would be 0.125 l.)

items.q: Convert. 750 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1,000: 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 750 g = 0.75 kg.

items.q: Convert. 2.375 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 2.375 × 1,000 = 2,375. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 2.375 kg = 2,375 g.

items.q: Convert. 0.5 l = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 0.5 × 1,000 = 500. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.5 l = 500 ml.

items.q: Convert. 330 ml = ☐ l
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1,000: 330 ÷ 1,000 = 0.33. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 330 ml = 0.33 l.

items.q: Convert. 45 g = ☐ kg
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Grams are smaller than kilograms, so divide by 1,000: 45 ÷ 1,000 = 0.045. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 45 g = 0.045 kg.

items.q: Convert. 4.08 kg = ☐ g
items.e: 1 kg = 1,000 g. Kilograms are bigger than grams, so multiply by 1,000: 4.08 × 1,000 = 4,080. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 4.08 kg = 4,080 g.

items.q: Convert. 0.2 l = ☐ ml
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Litres are bigger than millilitres, so multiply by 1,000: 0.2 × 1,000 = 200. The digits move 3 places to the left. So 0.2 l = 200 ml.

items.q: Convert. 2,600 ml = ☐ l
items.e: 1 l = 1,000 ml. Millilitres are smaller than litres, so divide by 1,000: 2,600 ÷ 1,000 = 2.6. The digits move 3 places to the right. So 2,600 ml = 2.6 l.

items.q: Convert. 3 kg 50 g = ☐ kg
Work out 1.5 kg + 700 g. Give your answer in kilograms.
items.e: Use one unit first: 700 g = 0.7 kg. Then 1.5 + 0.7 = 2.2 kg. 701.5 kg adds the numbers without converting.

items.q: Which is the heaviest?
items.e: Change them all to grams: 1.2 kg = 1,200 g, 0.95 kg = 950 g, 1 kg 150 g = 1,150 g. 1,200 g is the heaviest.

items.q: Which list goes from the smallest to the largest capacity?
items.e: Change them all to millilitres: 0.25 l = 250 ml and 0.5 l = 500 ml. 250 < 400 < 500.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 0.6 × 1,000 = 600, so 0.6 kg = 600 g. The others are wrong: 1.05 l = 1,050 ml, and 3 kg = 3,000 g, which is less than 3,100 g.

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a bag of flour. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 5 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 5 = 0.2 kg (200 g). The needle is 2 marks past 1 kg: 1 + 0.4 = 1.4 kg. (1.2 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of a parcel. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: Each kilogram is split into 4 equal spaces, so each mark is 1 ÷ 4 = 0.25 kg (250 g). The needle is 3 marks past 2 kg: 2 + 0.75 = 2.75 kg. (2.3 kg counts each mark as 0.1 kg.)

items.q: The scale shows the mass of some apples. What is the mass in kilograms?
items.e: The needle points to 600 g. 1 kg = 1,000 g, so divide by 1,000: 600 ÷ 1,000 = 0.6 kg.

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 500 ml and there are 5 spaces, so each line is 100 ml. The water is 3 lines above 1,000 ml: 1,300 ml. 1,300 ÷ 1,000 = 1.3 l.

items.q: How much water is in the jug? Give your answer in litres.
items.e: The numbers go up by 250 ml and there are 5 spaces, so each line is 50 ml. The water is 3 lines above 500 ml: 500 + 150 = 650 ml. 650 ÷ 1,000 = 0.65 l. (0.53 l counts each line as 10 ml.)

items.q: How much more water is needed to fill the jug to 2 litres?
items.e: Each line is 100 ml. The water is at 1,600 ml. 2 litres = 2,000 ml. 2,000 − 1,600 = 400 ml more.

sets.title: Time: decimals of hours, minutes and days

items.q: Which is the same as 2.5 hours?
items.e: 0.5 hours is half an hour, and half of 60 minutes is 30 minutes. So 2.5 hours = 2 hours 30 minutes. 2 hours 50 minutes treats an hour as 100 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 hours = ☐ minutes
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes. Multiply: 1.5 × 60 = 90, so 1.5 hours = 90 minutes (60 + 30).

items.q: Convert. 0.25 hours = ☐ minutes
items.e: 0.25 is one quarter. A quarter of 60 minutes is 60 ÷ 4 = 15 minutes. (0.25 × 60 = 15.)

items.q: Convert. 2.5 minutes = ☐ seconds
items.e: 1 minute = 60 seconds. Multiply: 2.5 × 60 = 150, so 2.5 minutes = 150 seconds (120 + 30).

items.q: Convert. 1 hour = ☐ seconds
items.e: 1 hour = 60 minutes and 1 minute = 60 seconds. 60 × 60 = 3,600, so 1 hour = 3,600 seconds.

items.q: Convert. 0.2 hours = ☐ minutes
items.e: 0.2 is two tenths. One tenth of 60 minutes is 60 ÷ 10 = 6 minutes, so two tenths is 2 × 6 = 12 minutes, not 20.

items.q: Convert. 4 days = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. Multiply: 4 × 24 = 96, so 4 days = 96 hours.

items.q: Convert. 72 hours = ☐ days
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours. Hours to days: divide. 72 ÷ 24 = 3, so 72 hours = 3 days. Do not divide by 10 (that gives 7.2).

items.q: Convert. 14 weeks = ☐ days
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. Multiply: 14 × 7 = 98, so 14 weeks = 98 days.

items.q: Convert. 63 days = ☐ weeks
items.e: 1 week = 7 days. Days to weeks: divide. 63 ÷ 7 = 9, so 63 days = 9 weeks.

items.q: Convert. 1 week = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 week = 7 days and 1 day = 24 hours. 7 × 24 = 168, so 1 week = 168 hours.

items.q: Convert. 1.5 days = ☐ hours
items.e: 1 day = 24 hours, and half a day is 12 hours. 24 + 12 = 36, so 1.5 days = 36 hours.

items.q: Convert. 3 hours 20 minutes = ☐ minutes
items.e: 3 hours = 3 × 60 = 180 minutes. Add the 20 minutes: 180 + 20 = 200 minutes.

items.q: Which is the same as 210 seconds?
items.e: 180 seconds = 3 minutes. 210 − 180 = 30, so 210 seconds = 3 minutes 30 seconds. (210 ÷ 60 = 3.5, but 0.5 minutes is 30 seconds, not 50.)

items.q: Which is the same as 3.75 hours?
items.e: 0.75 hours is three quarters of an hour: 0.75 × 60 = 45 minutes. So 3.75 hours = 3 hours 45 minutes.

items.q: Convert. 135 minutes = ☐ hours
items.e: 135 minutes = 120 + 15 minutes = 2 hours 15 minutes. 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, 0.25 hours. So 135 minutes = 2.25 hours, not 2.15 hours.

items.q: Which is the same as 45 days?
items.e: 6 × 7 = 42 days. 45 − 42 = 3 days left over, so 45 days = 6 weeks 3 days. The remainder is days, so it is not 6.3 weeks.

items.q: Which is the longest time?
items.e: Change them all to minutes: 1.2 hours = 1.2 × 60 = 72 minutes (not 1 hour 20 minutes), 1 hour 15 minutes = 75 minutes and 4,200 seconds = 4,200 ÷ 60 = 70 minutes. 78 minutes is the longest.

items.q: Which is true?
items.e: 0.75 × 60 = 45, so 0.75 hours = 45 minutes. 1.5 hours = 90 minutes, and 2.4 hours = 2 hours 24 minutes (0.4 × 60 = 24).

items.q: Find the missing number. 2.5 minutes − 45 seconds = ☐ seconds
items.e: 2.5 minutes = 2.5 × 60 = 150 seconds. 150 − 45 = 105 seconds. 205 seconds comes from treating 2.5 minutes as 250 seconds.

items.q: Approximately how many kilometres are the same as 5 miles?
items.e: This is the fact to learn: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. A mile is longer than a kilometre.

items.q: Approximately how many miles are the same as 8 km?
items.e: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. So 8 km is about 5 miles. There are fewer miles because a mile is longer.

items.q: Approximately how many kilometres are the same as 10 miles?
items.e: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. 10 miles is 2 lots of 5 miles, so it is about 2 × 8 = 16 km.

items.q: Approximately how many kilometres are the same as 40 miles?
items.e: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. 40 ÷ 5 = 8 lots, so 8 × 8 = 64 km. (25 km comes from going the wrong way.)

items.q: Approximately how many miles are the same as 24 km?
items.e: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. 24 ÷ 8 = 3 lots, so 3 × 5 = 15 miles. (3 miles forgets to multiply by 5.)

items.q: Approximately how many kilometres are the same as 25 miles?
items.e: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. 25 ÷ 5 = 5 lots, so 5 × 8 = 40 km.

items.q: Approximately how many miles are the same as 100 km?
items.e: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. 100 ÷ 8 = 12.5 lots, so 12.5 × 5 = 62.5 miles. Kilometres to miles: the number gets smaller.

items.q: Approximately how many kilometres are the same as 120 miles?
items.e: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. 120 ÷ 5 = 24 lots, so 24 × 8 = 192 km. (960 km multiplies by 8 but forgets to divide by 5.)

items.q: Approximately how many kilometres are the same as 2.5 miles?
items.e: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. 2.5 miles is half of 5 miles, so it is about half of 8 km = 4 km.

items.q: Which fact says the same as 5 miles ≈ 8 km?
items.e: Divide both sides by 5: 5 ÷ 5 = 1 mile and 8 ÷ 5 = 1.6 km. A mile is longer than a kilometre, so 1 mile is more than 1 km.

items.q: Approximately how many miles are the same as 1.6 km?
items.e: 1 mile ≈ 1.6 km (8 ÷ 5 = 1.6). So 1.6 km is about 1 mile.

items.q: Use the conversion graph. Approximately how many kilometres are the same as 30 miles?
items.e: Up from 30 miles to the line, then across: 48 km. On the km axis each square is 8 km (the labels go up in 16s), so 6 squares is 48 km, not 60 km.

items.q: Use the conversion graph. Approximately how many kilometres are the same as 45 miles?
items.e: Up from 45 miles (halfway between 40 and 50) to the line, then across: 72 km (halfway between 64 and 80). Each square on the km axis is 8 km.

items.q: Use the conversion graph. Approximately how many miles are the same as 56 km?
items.e: Across from 56 km to the line, then down: 35 miles (halfway between 30 and 40). Each square on the miles axis is 5 miles, so 7 squares is 35 miles, not 70.

items.q: Use the conversion graph. Approximately how many miles are the same as 40 km?
items.e: Across from 40 km to the line, then down: 25 miles (halfway between 20 and 30). Each square on the miles axis is 5 miles.

items.q: The double number line uses 5 miles ≈ 8 km. What is the missing number?
items.e: Each step on the top line is 5 miles, and each step on the bottom line is 8 km. 16 + 8 = 24, so 15 miles ≈ 24 km. (21 km adds 5 instead of 8.)

items.q: Which list goes from the shortest to the longest distance?
items.e: Change 15 miles to km: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 lots, 3 × 8 = 24 km. So 20 km < 24 km < 30 km.

items.q: A road sign says London 80 miles. Approximately how far is that in kilometres?
items.e: 5 miles is approximately 8 km. 80 ÷ 5 = 16 lots, so 16 × 8 = 128 km.

items.q: Zara cycles 30 miles. Charlie cycles 45 km. Who cycles further, and by about how much?
items.e: Use one unit. 30 miles: 30 ÷ 5 = 6 lots, 6 × 8 = 48 km. 48 km > 45 km, so Zara cycles further, by 48 − 45 = 3 km. 45 is the bigger number, but miles are longer than kilometres.

items.q: A marathon is about 42 km. Approximately how many miles is that, to the nearest mile?
items.e: Kilometres to miles: divide by 8, then multiply by 5. 42 ÷ 8 = 5.25 and 5.25 × 5 = 26.25, so about 26 miles. (67 miles goes the wrong way: 42 × 1.6.)

sets.title: Word problems: recipes, journeys and races

items.q: Grace makes pancakes. One batch needs 0.3 kg of flour. She makes 3 batches from a 1.5 kg bag. How many grams of flour are left?
items.e: 3 × 0.3 = 0.9 kg used. 1.5 − 0.9 = 0.6 kg left. 0.6 × 1,000 = 600 g. (1,200 g only takes away one batch.)

items.q: A recipe for 4 people uses 250 ml of milk. How many litres of milk are needed for 10 people?
items.e: 250 ÷ 4 = 62.5 ml for each person. 10 × 62.5 = 625 ml. 625 ÷ 1,000 = 0.625 l. (2.5 l uses 250 ml for each person.)

items.q: A biscuit recipe uses 125 g of butter to make 12 biscuits. Poppy wants to make 36 biscuits. How many kilograms of butter does she need?
A 2 litre carton of juice is poured into 8 glasses of 0.18 l. How many millilitres are left in the carton?
Ethan posts three parcels: 1.25 kg, 750 g and 2.4 kg. What is their total mass in kilograms?
items.e: Change 750 g to kilograms first: 750 ÷ 1,000 = 0.75 kg. 1.25 + 0.75 + 2.4 = 4.4 kg.

items.q: Charlie drinks 0.35 l of milk every day for 2 weeks. How much milk is that altogether?
items.e: 2 weeks = 14 days. 14 × 0.35 = 4.9 l. (2.45 l is only 1 week.)

items.q: Four pupils do a standing long jump. Oliver jumps 1.6 m, Ava jumps 155 cm, Leo jumps 1,580 mm and Isla jumps 1.06 m. Who jumps the furthest?
items.e: Change them all to centimetres: 1.6 m = 160 cm, 1,580 mm = 158 cm and 1.06 m = 106 cm. 160 cm is the furthest, so Oliver jumps the furthest.

items.q: Evie swims 1.2 km in a 25 m pool. How many lengths does she swim?
A school 5 km fun run goes round a 400 m track. How many laps is that?
items.e: 5 km = 5,000 m. 5,000 ÷ 400 = 12.5 laps. Check: 12 × 400 = 4,800 m and half a lap is 200 m more.

items.q: A 1.5 km relay race is split into 4 equal legs. How long is each leg in metres?
items.e: 1.5 km = 1,500 m. 1,500 ÷ 4 = 375 m. (0.375 m is the answer in kilometres written with the wrong unit.)

items.q: Noah runs 4 laps of the playground. Each lap takes 1 minute 45 seconds. How long does he run for?
items.e: 1 minute 45 seconds = 105 seconds. 4 × 105 = 420 seconds. 420 ÷ 60 = 7 minutes. (5 minutes 80 seconds works out 4 × 1.45 as if a minute had 100 seconds.)

items.q: A film starts at 6:45 pm. It lasts 2.25 hours. What time does it finish?
items.e: 2.25 hours = 2 hours 15 minutes (0.25 × 60 = 15). 6:45 pm + 2 hours = 8:45 pm, and 15 more minutes is 9:00 pm. (9:10 pm uses 25 minutes.)

items.q: Mohammed practises the piano for 25 minutes every day for 3 weeks. How long is that altogether?
items.e: 3 weeks = 21 days. 21 × 25 = 525 minutes. 8 × 60 = 480, and 525 − 480 = 45, so it is 8 hours 45 minutes, not 5 hours 25 minutes.

items.q: A sponsored walk is 12 km. The class walks 2.75 km before lunch and 3,600 m after lunch. How much further do they still have to walk?
Isla has 4.5 m of ribbon. She cuts it into pieces 15 cm long. How many pieces does she get?
items.e: 4.5 m = 450 cm. 450 ÷ 15 = 30 pieces. (3 pieces divides 45 by 15 without converting.)

items.q: Ruby's family drives 45 miles to a theme park, then 32 km to a hotel. Approximately how far do they drive altogether in kilometres?
items.e: 45 miles: 45 ÷ 5 = 9 lots, 9 × 8 = 72 km. 72 + 32 = 104 km. (77 km adds miles and kilometres as if they were the same.)

items.q: A sign says Bristol 40 miles. Zara's family then drives 24 km towards Bristol. Approximately how many miles do they still have to go?
items.e: 24 km: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 lots, 3 × 5 = 15 miles. 40 − 15 = 25 miles to go. (16 miles takes away 24 without converting.)

items.q: Aisha's family drives 150 miles to the coast. They stop for lunch after 80 km. Approximately how many more miles do they have to drive?
items.e: 80 km: 80 ÷ 8 = 10 lots, 10 × 5 = 50 miles. 150 − 50 = 100 miles. (22 miles changes 80 km the wrong way, into 128.)

items.q: A 60-mile charity cycle ride is split into 4 equal stages. Approximately how long is each stage in kilometres?
items.e: 60 ÷ 4 = 15 miles in each stage. 15 ÷ 5 = 3 lots, 3 × 8 = 24 km. (96 km is the whole ride, not one stage.)

items.q: Put these distances in order from shortest to longest: 3 miles, 4.5 km, 4,900 m.
items.e: Change them all to metres. 3 miles ≈ 3 × 1.6 = 4.8 km = 4,800 m, and 4.5 km = 4,500 m. 4,500 < 4,800 < 4,900.
